body:
I'm not sure constantly creating and deleting `AudioStreamPlayer` is a good idea from an optimization standpoint. We could use the `AudioStreamPlayer.max_polyphony` property, the new `AudioStreamPolyphonic`, or some other approach on the `AudioServer` side. Here are two options I've used in my projects for adding sound effects:

<details>
<summary>AudioStreamPlayer.max_polyphony</summary>

```gdscript
extends Node

var _players: Dictionary[String, AudioStreamPlayer]

func play(path: String) -> void:
    var player: AudioStreamPlayer = _players.get(path)
    if not player:
        player = AudioStreamPlayer.new()
        player.bus = &"SFX"
        player.stream = load(path)
        player.max_polyphony = 4
        add_child(player)
        _players[path] = player
    player.play()
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>AudioStreamPolyphonic</summary>

```gdscript
extends Node

var _playback: AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic
var _streams: Dictionary[String, AudioStream]

func _ready() -> void:
    var player: AudioStreamPlayer = AudioStreamPlayer.new()
    player.bus = &"SFX"
    player.stream = AudioStreamPolyphonic.new()
    #player.stream.polyphony = 32
    add_child(player)

    player.play()
    _playback = player.get_stream_playback()

func play(path: String) -> void:
    var stream: AudioStream = _streams.get(path)
    if not stream:
        stream = load(path)
        _streams[path] = stream
    _playback.play_stream(stream)
```

</details>

I feel like this PR should heavily depend on a corresponding server API that creates audio stream playbacks. This has been needed and proposed many times in the past. In this particular case it would heavily benefit it.
